points.title: Southmere Lake
points.description: Southmere Lake appears in A Clockwork Orange as part of the film’s unsettling, open urban landscape. Built as part of a utopian post-war housing vision, Thamesmead was designed to bring light, space, and modernity to Londoners. On screen, however, the same openness becomes alienating.

audio.title: Title Music (A Clockwork Orange)
audio.note: Press play as you approach the lake. Let the music settle before you start walking.

points.title: Binsey Walk Elevated Pathways
points.description: These elevated walkways were designed to separate pedestrians from traffic, a hallmark of modernist urban planning. In practice, they became empty corridors of movement.

audio.title: Wendy Carlos - Timesteps
audio.note: Play as you walk along the pathway. Keep a steady pace and notice the repetition of the architecture.

points.title: Tavy Bridge
points.description: Tavy Bridge is one of the most recognisable locations from A Clockwork Orange. Its stark concrete symmetry creates a visually controlled environment.

audio.title: Beethoven - Symphony No. 9 (2nd Movement)
audio.note: Start just before stepping onto the bridge. Let the scale of the space match the intensity of the music.

points.title: Coralline Walk Housing Blocks
points.description: In Brazil, similar housing estates are used to depict a world dominated by bureaucracy and impersonal systems.

audio.title: Brazil Theme (Aquarela do Brasil)
audio.note: This is intentionally ironic — cheerful music against an oppressive environment. Let that contrast sink in.

points.title: Thamesmead Waterfront
points.description: Children of Men uses locations like Thamesmead by layering subtle signs of control and decay onto familiar environments.

audio.title: Children of Men - 'Fragments of a Prayer'
audio.note: Play at the waterfront. This is a moment to slow down and reflect before ending the walk.
